items.title: George "Jug" Jernberg Interview, 1963-08-23
items.q: Well, you said that Louie and Oliver performed pretty much by themselves.

ctx.x: Yes, very good. I was trying to think of his name just last night, I think. He had a style of clarinet playing that was very, very nice, very soft and subdued, but very nice clarinet playing. He used to work at the old Apex Club on 35th Street. Yes, he was a very nice clarinet player. Yes. He was a clarinet player. But I'll say this. We'll get back to Johnny Dodds again. That guy was strictly a New Orleans jazz clarinet player, but brother, his instrument always sounded like a clarinet. Yeah. Always sounded like…
Well, you said that Louie and Oliver performed pretty much by themselves. That's right, the same way. How does it sound like an integrated band? And by integrated, I just mean it was.
Yeah. No, those bands in those days sounded pretty rough and, you know, there should have been just a little bit of refinement about the sound.
